subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: Hi, I'm 48 years old and female. I'm here because my right finger has been hurting since I was skiing over the weekend. I think I bent it back when I went over a mogul. Doctor: Could you please confirm your age, gender, and describe the pain in your right finger, including when it started, its intensity, and any associated symptoms? Patient: Sure. The pain started on Sunday after I was skiing and I bent my finger back when I went over a mogul. It's been hurting a lot, especially when I move it, and even putting ice on it and taking ibuprofen hasn't really helped much. It's pretty painful still. Doctor: Have you noticed any swelling, deformity, or inability to move your right finger since the injury? Patient: No, I haven't noticed any swelling or deformity, but it does hurt when I move it. Patient: No, I haven't had any numbness, tingling, or weakness in my finger or hand since the injury. It's just been painful, especially when I move it. Doctor: Have you had any prior imaging or evaluation of the right finger since the injury occurred? Patient: No, I haven't had any prior imaging or evaluation of my right finger since the injury occurred. This is the first time I've been seen about it. Doctor: Have you noticed any instability or 'popping' sensation in the finger when moving it, or any difficulty gripping objects since the injury? Patient: No, I haven't noticed any instability or popping sensation in the finger when moving it, and I haven't had any difficulty gripping objects since the injury.
